_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG05-FG14_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — the copy pulled from the client's Google Drive on 2026-09-16. FG-13 'Background Job Platform' holds 6 cases: TC-JOB-002, -003, -004, -006, -015, -016. All 6 are implemented.
_target: Odoo 19 only. The v15 database carried the connector's own bundled job code, not the OCA queue_job app these cases navigate.
_safety: Two facts shape every test here. (1) queue.job.create is @api.private (queue_job/models/queue_job.py:269) — confirmed against the target, the call returns AccessError — and queue_job/security/ir.model.access.csv grants the manager group perm_read,perm_write and NOT perm_create/perm_unlink. So this platform cannot craft a job of its own. (2) The job runner is live on this instance: odoo19.conf carries server_wide_modules = base,web,queue_job and the container log reads 'queue job runner ready for db mmg'. A job moved back to pending is executed within seconds. The only jobs on the database are the client's own (3,148 rows, 1,727 failed), so pressing Requeue on one would re-run real connector work against the client's acceptance database. requeue() is therefore never called.
_probe: button_done and button_cancelled ARE called, on a job already in state 'done'. Both open with self.filtered(lambda job_: job_.state in states_from) (queue_job.py:333-348) and 'done' is in neither tuple, so the call resolves to an empty recordset and writes nothing. That is precisely the point: TC-JOB-003's Expected Result line 4 says an already-successful job 'must not silently re-run', and the probe reads the state back afterwards either way. requeue is NOT probed this way — its states_from legitimately includes 'done'.
_residual_manual: Pressing Requeue Job and reading the state back (TC-JOB-002 steps 10-11); the requeue wizard end to end (TC-JOB-003 steps 5-9); pressing Set to 'Done' and Cancel job on the client's failed jobs, which the workbook's own precondition says Novobi must nominate (TC-JOB-004 steps 4-10); looking at the apps menu with the second login's own eyes (TC-JOB-016 step 5, asserted here through the same ir.ui.menu.load_menus the web client calls).

_findings.OBS-FG13-001: TC-JOB-003 step 10 asks what the requeue action does to a DONE job selected alongside a failed one, and its Expected Result allows 'either leaves it alone or is refused'. The shipped behaviour is neither: queue.job.requeue's states_from is (failed, done, cancelled), so a done job IS moved back to pending, and the wizard does not filter by state either (queue_job/wizards/queue_requeue_job.py:22). Not a porting regression — v15 behaved the same way — but Novobi should decide whether it is acceptable. Recorded by TEST-FG13-JOB-003, which PASSES: the assertion it makes is the workbook's, about button_done/button_cancelled leaving a done job alone, and that holds.
_findings.OBS-FG13-002: queue.job.function rows on the database exceed what the modules' data files declare (omni_manage_channel 3 vs 2, multichannel_order 11 vs 8). queue.job.function._register_job creates a row the first time with_delay() reaches an undeclared method and attributes it to the owning module, so TC-JOB-006 asserts a shortfall rather than equality. Both counts are exported as CSV artifacts.
_findings.OBS-FG13-003: v19 renamed the groups relation from groups_id to group_ids on res.users, ir.ui.menu and the action models. Reading the v15 name RAISES rather than returning an empty list, so a test written against it would look like a product defect. Resolved at run time here. Also: ir.ui.menu.search is NOT group-filtered in v19 — visibility is decided by _filter_visible_menus inside load_menus (odoo/addons/base/models/ir_ui_menu.py:236-244) — so TC-JOB-016 asks the question the browser asks.

TC-JOB-002.reason: The five menus and the group gating them, the Jobs action's five pre-applied filters and the two it deliberately omits, the list columns, a real failed job's fields and its Exception Info, the status bar, and all three header buttons with their gating expressions. Step 10 is residual manual.

TC-JOB-003.reason: The three Actions-menu wizards, their bindings and their dialog target, plus the complement (no fourth bound action). Step 10 is probed for real against a done job. Steps 5-9 are residual manual.

TC-JOB-004.reason: Both buttons offered on a failed job and gated away on a started one, in the view and in the states_from tuples; Done and Cancelled as genuinely different states each with its own single-state filter; and the state names written down for FG-14 as step 12 asks. The presses are residual manual.

TC-JOB-006.reason: Every module's declared functions present, the spread across channels, every retry pattern parsed as attempt->delay, the channel tree and its parents, and the root channel refusing a rename through queue.job.channel.write — a refusal that rolls itself back. Both tables exported as CSV. The workbook's 'baseline from the old system' is stood in for by what the installed modules declare, because the v15 database is empty.

TC-JOB-015.reason: Writes to the client's database — a logged note and a scheduled activity on one job record — because 'does a note survive a reload' is a question about a round trip, not about a view definition. Both are marked and removed in a finally, and the case asserts nothing is left behind.

TC-JOB-016.reason: The one FG-13 case testable end to end. The second login the workbook asks Novobi to prepare is created here, in base.group_user only, and removed in a finally; every assertion is a refusal, and the manager's own access is re-checked afterwards so the negative result cannot pass for the wrong reason.
